title: Wi-Fi says Connected but there's no internet
summary: Your PC joined the Wi-Fi network but websites and apps won't load. Resetting Windows' network settings fixes most cases.
cause: Either the router or modem has stalled, or Windows' network settings (its address, DNS cache or network stack) got stuck.
steps: Check another device on the same Wi-Fi. If it has no internet either, unplug your modem and router for 30 seconds, plug them back in, and wait two minutes.
Restart your PC. Turn off any VPN while testing.
Run the built-in fixer: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Internet Connections > Run.
Open Terminal (Admin) and run these one at a time: ipconfig /release, ipconfig /renew, ipconfig /flushdns, netsh winsock reset, netsh int ip reset. Restart afterward.
Reinstall the adapter driver: Device Manager > Network adapters > right-click your Wi-Fi adapter > Uninstall device, then restart. Windows reinstalls it.
ifStillBroken: As a last step, use Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It removes saved Wi-Fi networks, so keep your Wi-Fi password handy.

links.text: Microsoft: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows
links.note: Source for the command steps and Network reset. Microsoft says Network reset should be the last step.
